name: 03 · Request investigation — Production
description: Production request investigation: one log table for general/error/trace-ID searches, merged endpoint percentile and error-ratio charts, and gateway flags. Pod/severity/trace filters scope logs; API route scopes endpoint metrics. Stored spans remain unavailable. Rolling last 15m with 30s refresh.

filters.name: Trace ID
filters.where: $__filter(cluster_name, $cluster) AND $__filter(namespace_name, $namespace) AND $__filter(deployment_name, $deployment) AND $__filter(pod_name, $pod) AND coalesce(nullIf(trace_id, ''), nullIf(json_payload['trace_id'], ''), nullIf(extract(json_payload['logging.googleapis.com/trace'], '[^/]+$'), '')) != ''

config.name: Debugging workflow
config.markdown:
[01 · P0 overview](https://hyperdx.platform.prd.msgsndr.net/dashboards/6aa7af64466e0dad178178c4) · [02 · Capacity and startup](https://hyperdx.platform.prd.msgsndr.net/dashboards/e8ec27ebca8ec9510cc54010) · [03 · Request investigation](https://hyperdx.platform.prd.msgsndr.net/dashboards/8da8d7cbb9ebeb140a048e6f)

**Follow the request:** narrow API route for endpoint metrics, then Pod / Log level / Trace ID for logs. Route does not filter the log table; log filters do not filter endpoint metrics. Select error severity for error logs, or a Trace ID for correlated logs in the same table. Production has no configured stored-span source; correlated logs are not a span waterfall. Keep timestamp order for live logs and narrow the range before sorting other columns.

Navigation opens the saved view of the destination; it does not automatically carry unsaved filters or time. **Contacts incident · 12 September, 8:25–10:25 PM IST:** config.name: Gateway failures · HTTP 0 / 5xx by service and flag
How to read request evidence
config.markdown:
Gateway and endpoint rates use rolling 5m; gateway error counts use rolling 15m. Error-log count uses the selected dashboard range. Gateway failure flags: **UH** = no healthy upstream; **UF** = connection failure; **URX** = retry/connection-attempt limit; **UT** = timeout; **UC** = terminated connection. HTTP 0 is shown separately from 5xx. Caller retries can amplify RPM; requests are not unique users. Select a narrow route to avoid truncating the combined percentile chart (40-series limit). Reporting endpoints counts instrumented route/ownership combinations, not Kubernetes ready endpoints.

Logs use the selected cluster/namespace/deployment/pod/severity/trace ID. Stored-span and dependency-specific tracing remain a telemetry gap, not evidence of healthy dependencies. Caller RPM uses application sourceContainer labels and includes retries; it does not prove the originating campaign or unique business demand. Top callers can change during the time range; the chart displays at most 40 series.

**Contacts incident:** email-related callers account for about 88% of the measured onset increase on `/contacts/:contactId` in the separate 2-minute-rate comparison (8:30 → 8:32:30 PM). This is a caller-attribution lead, not proof of retries or a caller defect. The top-callers chart uses 5-minute rates and the selected route; gateway and application counters measure different observation points.
